title: External Secant and Tangent Angles Practice
description: Practice applying exterior angle relationships for secants and tangents.

questions.question: Two secants form an exterior angle. The intercepted arcs are 140° and 60°. What is the angle measure?
A tangent and a secant form an exterior angle. The intercepted arcs are 200° and 80°. What is the angle measure?
Two tangents are drawn from the same exterior point. The minor arc between the tangent points is 110°. What is the exterior angle?
questions.explanation: For two tangents, the angle is 180 - minor arc = 180 - 110 = 70°.

questions.question: An exterior angle formed by two secants equals half the sum of the intercepted arcs.
questions.explanation: Exterior secant and tangent angles use half the difference, not half the sum.

questions.question: Two secants form an exterior angle with intercepted arcs 156° and 44°. Enter the angle measure in degrees.
An exterior tangent-secant angle is 30°. The smaller intercepted arc is 70°. What is the larger intercepted arc?
Two tangents form an exterior angle of 48°. Enter the minor arc measure in degrees.
questions.explanation: For two tangents, angle = 180 - minor arc. So 48 = 180 - x, and x = 132°.

questions.question: A student sees arcs 170° and 50° and answers 110° for the exterior angle. Explain the mistake and give the correct angle.
questions.correctAnswer: The student likely subtracted but forgot to take half. The correct angle is 1/2(170 - 50) = 60°.
questions.explanation: Exterior angle problems require half the difference of the intercepted arcs.
